claims.claim: Species formula: the child is the species whose hidden breeding number (CombiRank) is closest to the parents' average, rounded up; exact ties go to the higher number
claims.evidence: Verified at code level in palcalc (open-source solver generated from the game files) and replayed here against all 44,851 precomputed 1.0 results with zero mismatches.

claims.claim: Tie-break: on an exact tie the higher CombiRank wins (a 1.0 change)
claims.evidence: All 14,021 tie pairs in the 1.0 oracle resolve to the higher rank (0 exceptions); the game field CombiDuplicatePriority = CombiRank×100. Old wiki text ('lowest index') is stale Early Access wording. Also matches the player test Turtacle+Aegidron→Nitemary.

claims.claim: Unique-recipe children are excluded from the generic pool (183 species remain)
claims.evidence: palcalc filters every DT_PalCombiUnique child out of the pool; with this model all 44,851 results match, without it 14,699 pairs mispredict. palworld.gg's ignoreCombi-39 model is wrong for 1.0.

claims.claim: Katress+Wixen is the game's only gender-dependent pair
claims.evidence: Exactly 2 gender-specific rows out of 44,851: female Katress + male Wixen → Katress Ignis; female Wixen + male Katress → Wixen Noct.

claims.claim: Same species + same species always yields that species
claims.evidence: Short-circuits in the game code before any other logic; 299/299 self-pairs in the oracle confirm it.

claims.claim: "164 unique combinations" (the paldb view)
claims.evidence: The game's raw table has 258 rows in total (many redundant X+X=X rows and event content). The 136 cross rows match paldb exactly — those are what the plan uses (134 regular + 2 gender-dependent). "164" is paldb's display choice, not wrong data.

claims.claim: The EA recipes for Lyleen, Grizzbolt, Faleris, Orserk and Shadowbeak were removed in 1.0
claims.evidence: Verified against the game's raw table using internal IDs: none of the five old pairs exist; all five species only have a self-pair row. (Mossanda+Grizzbolt=Mossanda Lux was kept, though.)

claims.claim: Condenser 1.0: 48 copies to 4★, split 4/8/12/24
claims.evidence: Patch-note recaps and several independent guides confirm 116→48; the per-star split matches the in-game player measurement. Note: Starfruit (Dog Coins) can substitute for copies.

claims.claim: Stars: +1 work suitability per star, 4★ raises all, partner skill = stars+1
claims.evidence: Confirmed in patch notes and wiki — but the 'best job first' order at intermediate stars is NOT confirmed anywhere; the game only says 'one of its suitabilities'.

claims.claim: Cake tiers: Cake 17 / Mushroom 30 / Vegetable 47 / Extravagant 60 / Special 74
claims.evidence: Tech levels, stations and effects confirmed by several sources (one outlier on the Special tier; the majority says 74).

claims.claim: Mutation chance: ~1% base, ~3% with Extravagant Vegetable Cake
claims.evidence: Confirmed — but the Vegetable Cake does NOT give 2% per egg: it gives 2 eggs at 1% each (≈2% per cycle). The earlier session's figure was imprecise on this point.

claims.claim: Mutant eggs: hatch as Alpha with 2★, IVs ~91–100, at least 2 rainbow passives
claims.evidence: 2★ and Alpha status confirmed; '4 passives, at least 2 rainbow' per the wiki (not all are mutation-exclusive); the 91–100 IV range is guide consensus, the wiki only says 'very high'.

claims.claim: The 5 rainbow passives: Immortality, Idiosyncratic, Babysitter, Heavily Armored, Skymarcher
claims.evidence: The exact same five on the wiki, game8 and paldb; 'Skirmisher' does not exist. They can be inherited onward through normal breeding once a parent has them.

claims.claim: Work suitability goes to 10 with exponential scaling (Lv5=400 … Lv10=5400)
claims.evidence: The Handiwork value table (50/80/140/240/400/680/1100/1900/3200/5400) confirmed by several independent sources.

claims.claim: Pal Surgery Table (tech 38): implant passives for gold, implants not consumed
claims.evidence: Tech 38 confirmed; 10–50k gold per operation depending on rarity; standard implants are reusable (1.0 also has disposable implants from World Tree relics).

claims.claim: The Pal Reverser swaps gender
claims.evidence: An item (not a station) used at the operating table; consumed on use; bought with Bounty Tokens / Battle Tickets and more.

claims.claim: IV inheritance: 30% father / 30% mother / 40% random per stat
claims.evidence: Confirmed by several sources incl. the arithmetic 0.6³ ≈ 21.6% for triple-100 with two perfect parents.

claims.claim: Passive inheritance ~24% male / ~20% female per slot
claims.evidence: All sources cite the same small EA-era dataset (~100 eggs); datamining suggests a different underlying mechanism (pooled draw). The direction 'male inherits more often' holds.

claims.claim: "10 species have no wild spawns" (from the earlier session)
claims.evidence: DEBUNKED: all ten (Solenne, Renjishi, Univolt Cryst, Mycora, Venusa etc.) can be caught in the World Tree region (lvl 75+) as regular spawns or field bosses. 1.0 removed the breed-only category. At lvl 44, breeding is still the realistic route.

claims.claim: Astralym cannot be obtained in 1.0
claims.evidence: Story boss; cannot be caught, does not exist as an alpha, and is not a reward.

claims.claim: All 12 aura pals (+1 work suitability to the base) check out
claims.evidence: All twelve confirmed per species (Ribbuny, Tetroise, Wumpo, Amione, Cinnamoth, Clovee, Eikthyrdeer Terra, Katress Ignis, Mycora, Petallia, Puffolt, Smokie Cryst). Never buffs the carrier, does not stack, works from the base. Oil Extraction has no aura.

claims.claim: Sekhmet boosts Anubis; Braloha speeds up eggs; Dynamoff cuts incubation time
claims.evidence: Sekhmet's real skill is 'Desert Empress': Anubis work speed +20–40% (+ own workbench bonus). Braloha 'Balmy Weather': egg production +20–50%. Dynamoff 'Electro-Massage Incubation': incubation −20–40%.

claims.claim: Level cap 80; Breeding Farm tech 19; 299 species total
claims.evidence: Level cap 65→80 confirmed. Breeding Farm tech 19 (2 tech points). Species count: 287 Paldeck entries + the Terraria crossover (Sealed Realm of Terraria dungeon, all rank 3100) ≈ the dataset's 299; Astralym is unobtainable.

claims.claim: Passive inheritance count is weighted 40/30/20/10 for drawing 1/2/3/4 passives from the parents' combined de-duplicated pool
claims.evidence: GameSettings.PassiveInheritNum = [4,3,2,1], read from the game files by palcalc's DB generator (PalCalc.GenDB/BuildDBProgram.cs, PalCalc.Model/db.json). Matches palworld.wiki.gg/Breeding's published mechanic.

claims.claim: Random extra passives are an independent roll weighted 40/30/20/10 for adding 0/1/2/3 new passives, capped at 4 total slots
claims.evidence: GameSettings.PassiveRandomAddNum = [4,3,2,1] over 0..3 (same source). The engine's closed-form model built on these weights reproduces the community's measured 40/24/12/10 clean-inheritance table exactly (app/tests/odds.test.ts) and matches a 200k-egg Monte Carlo simulation.

claims.claim: IV/talent inheritance takes 1/2/3 stat categories from the parents with weights 3/2/1 (50%/33.3%/16.7%); at least one is always inherited; each inherited category picks mother or father 50/50
claims.evidence: GameSettings.TalentInheritNum = [3,2,1] (same game-file source); community's '30/30/40 per stat' model (Austin John Gaming testing, palworld.wiki.gg) is the same distribution seen per-category.

claims.claim: Vegetable Cake gives 2 eggs per cycle at the base ~1% mutation rate each (a throughput gain, not a 2% rate); Extravagant Vegetable Cake raises mutation to ~3% per egg
claims.evidence: paldb.cc/en/Mutation (2026-07-18) and in-game item descriptions. The game's DA_BreedingItemEffectData table has not been published field-by-field, so cake numbers are community-measured, not datamined.

claims.claim: Special Cake overrides the number of passives drawn from the parents (reported up to 6 carried)
claims.evidence: In-game item description ('more likely to inherit multiple passive skills') + PassiveInheritCountOverride field name visible in palcalc's notes on DA_BreedingItemEffectData; exact override value not published.

claims.claim: Five mutation-exclusive passives exist (Immortality, Idiosyncratic, Babysitter, Heavily Armored, Skymarcher); once obtained they are inheritable like normal passives
claims.evidence: paldb.cc/en/Mutation lists all five with inheritability; cross-checked against beliarance/palworld-kb passives dataset (mutation_exclusive flags).

claims.claim: Partner-effect texts are complete and current across all 297 species (checked 2026-08-18)
claims.evidence: Every partner_effect diffed against paldb.cc's live game-table mirror by tools/fetch_partner_effects.py + the E140 sweep: 19 truncated/placeholder entries completed under a strict prefix rule (our text must be a character-prefix of the fetched text), 28 stale pre-1.0.3 wordings refreshed after per-entry hand review — including three real errors (Pengullet Lux's mechanic printed backwards, Tetroise Primo's durability effect, Mimog's missing limit sentence). 169 formatting-only differences left as-is. Snock Lux could not be re-verified (its paldb page carries no description tag) and stands as delivered. Diffs recorded in the ledger, E139-E140.
sources: paldb.cc per-pal pages (live game-table mirror, fetched 2026-08-18)

claims.claim: Helper-pal partner skills (planner recommendations) are game text: Chikipi egg / Mozzarina milk / Beegarde honey / Caprity berries ranch drops; Braloha breeding-farm speed; Dynamoff incubation cut; Grintale extra egg on pickup; Broncherry + Broncherry Aqua alpha-egg chance; Ribbuny base handiwork aura
claims.evidence: All ten effects quoted near-verbatim from partner_effect in pals_1_0.json (beliarance/palworld-kb dump of the game files, 2026-07-20 extraction, revalidated against patch 1.0.3 notes). Registry: engine/helpers.ts, recorded 2026-08-15.

claims.claim: Map projection: world coordinates are placed on the game's map texture with the game's own DT_WorldMapUIData bounds (Palpagos X -1099400..349400, Y -724400..724400; World Tree X 347351.5..689148.5, Y -818197..-476400), NOT palcalc's WorldToImageMatrix
claims.evidence: tools/verify_map_projection.py, reproducible. (1) Both regions are EXACTLY square (1,448,800 and 341,797 uu) matching square textures and mapping to [0,1] exactly, while palcalc's fitted matrix implies a region 8,711 uu out of square. (2) It wins a land-fit test over 58,504 datamined non-Water spawn points (86.86% vs 86.85%). (3) Residual bounded at 6 px of 4096 = 1.5 px at display size. (4) Cross-checked on a SECOND upstream's land-locked layers: 96.1% of fast-travel statues, 98.1% of dungeons and 100% of merchants land within 6 px of land. (5) All 79,714 points from both upstreams project inside [0,1] with zero exceptions.

claims.claim: Map spawn data: 68,617 wild spawn points across 250 species, each with a level band and whether that band is night-only
claims.evidence: Extracted from DT_PalSpawnerPlacement + DT_PalWildSpawner via Awy64/palworld-atlas-data build 24575149 (a CI runner that downloads the OFFICIAL anonymous Palworld dedicated-server package, schema-validates and publishes; never commits game assets). Count matches its manifest exactly. 272 of 273 upstream pal names match our 299-pal Paldex verbatim. Guarded by app/tests/map.test.ts (114-test suite).

claims.claim: The in-game map coordinate READOUT is translX 123930, translY 157935, scale 458.52 — so the numbers the app shows match the numbers on the player's screen
claims.evidence: Three independent projects agree: palcalc's WorldToMapMatrix, pal-atlas's GAME_READOUT, and palworld-atlas-data's own mapX/mapY column. Worked example locked in a unit test: alpha Anubis at world (-167230, 96430) -> readout (-134, -94) under all three.

claims.claim: NOT datamined truth: 115 Pengullet spawn rows carry LvMin 35 > LvMax 34 in the game's own spawner table; we re-order the pair so the UI reads 'Lv 34-35'
claims.evidence: Found by app/tests/map.test.ts asserting ordered level bands, traced to the source rows in palworld-atlas-data build 24575149. tools/extract_map_data.py swaps the pair and prints the count on every run, so the correction is never silent.

claims.claim: NOT the game's English name: palworld-atlas-data calls ElecSnail_Ground 'Snock Terra' (synthesised from the id suffix). The 1.0 game name is 'Snock Lux'
claims.evidence: paldb.cc, game8 and the Palworld wiki all give 'Snock Lux' for the Electric/Ground World Tree variant, despite the suffix convention implying Terra. tools/extract_map_data.py maps it by palId through PAL_ID_OVERRIDES rather than trusting the upstream display name.

claims.claim: Each fixed boss is its own row in the game's parameter table with its own stats (e.g. boss Paladius: HP 156 vs 130, size XL vs L, x1.855 fight HP, takes 18% of incoming damage; boss Lamball: HP 84 vs 70, size M vs XS)
claims.evidence: 205 of 207 titled fixed bosses fetched from paldb.cc per-boss pages (the raw DT_PalMonsterParameter row each; the table's existence and 753-row count confirmed by the palworld-atlas-data build manifest). Every row was accepted only when its CombiRank matched our oracle-tested value for the species; the 2 drops are recorded (Jolthog's boss page absent upstream; the Panthalus line is player-reported, not a boss page). Full capture with drop list: data/alpha_stats_1_0.json.
sources: paldb.cc per-boss pages, fetched 2026-08-18 (raw game-table mirror)
